title: The .michi file format and the michi binary
body: Design agreed 2026-10-08 and recorded in docs/file-format.md. syntax.michi at the project root is the worked example. The parser comes first, then highlighting, then the CLI.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/a556920e
Jack Roddy/a556920e
Jack Roddy/a556920e
notes.text:
Design: lexical rules. Agreed 2026-10-08.

Newlines mean nothing anywhere. A statement ends at `;` or at a block.

- `//` starts a comment to end of line, outside command text only.
- Strings are double quoted. Raw strings are `r#"…"#` and carry no escapes.
- Numbers are bare: `8`, `7.5`. A duration is a number with a unit suffix,
  one of `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`: `30s`, `500ms`, `1h`. No compound forms.
- A bare identifier names an enum variant, in snake case: `spread`,
  `first_touch`, `on_failure`.
- Reserved words, which no name or data key may use: `data`, `pipeline`,
  `step`, `let`, `def`, `fn`, `for`, `in`, `if`, `else`, `use`, `import`,
  `include`, `true`, `false`. Only the first three mean anything yet.
- A dotted path, `quick.N`, names a value in a data block.
- `$N` names a sweep variable.
- A shebang on line one, `#!/usr/bin/env michi`, is skipped.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/a556920e
notes.text:
Design: files, data blocks and pipelines. Agreed 2026-10-08.

A file holds data blocks and one or more pipelines, in any order.

```
data NAME {
    X = [5, 10, 15];
    Y = "tmp/err";
}
```

A data block names a group of lists and scalars. A block at the top of the
file is visible to every pipeline in it, one inside a pipeline only there.
Two blocks of one name in one scope is an error. A value is referenced by
path, `NAME.X`, in any value position, and a scalar also in command text
as `${NAME.X}`, which is not valid shell and so cannot collide with it.

A list holds numbers, identifiers, strings, tuples, and ranges. A range is
one element and splices among the others:

| form | gives |
| --- | --- |
| `0..5` | 0 1 2 3 4 |
| `0..=5` | 0 1 2 3 4 5 |
| `0..100:5` | 0 5 10 … 95 |
| `1..=16:*2` | 1 2 4 8 16 |
| `0.0..=1.0:0.1` | 0.0 0.1 … 1.0 |
| `[1, 2, 4..=8, 16]` | 1 2 4 5 6 7 8 16 |

michi computes a float range as `start + i × step`, so it reaches the end
by count and not by accumulation, and it prints each value with as many
decimal places as the step or the start has, whichever is more, so `0.1`
steps print `0.3` and never `0.30000000000000004`. A literal float prints
as written.

```
#[pool(8)]
pipeline NAME { … }
```

A pipeline holds data blocks, steps and parameter-list blocks. Its
attributes are the pipeline builder's methods. A parameter list may not
wrap a pipeline.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/a556920e
notes.text:
Design: attributes. Agreed 2026-10-08.

```
#[jobs(3), cores(2)]
#[on_error(continue)]
step burn { … }
```

An attribute line binds to the item or command below it. Several
attributes go in one `#[…]` separated by commas, or stack on separate
lines, and the two forms mean the same thing. A trailing comma is allowed
in every comma-separated list. A flag attribute takes no
parentheses: `#[no_stderr]`. Each attribute maps to one builder method,
under the builder's own name except where the tables below say otherwise.
michi rejects an attribute on the wrong kind of item, `jobs` on a command
or `timeout` on a step, at load. An attribute above a sweep block applies
to each item directly inside the block, before the item's own attributes,
so the item's own win.

Arguments are positional, or `key = value` where the builder takes a key.
A `$N` may stand in any argument, and is typed after substitution, so
`cores($T)` works and `cores(a)` fails at load naming the point.

### Pipeline

| attribute | builder | arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pool(n)` | `pool` | integer |
| `placement(v)` | `placement` | `pack`, `spread` |
| `stderr_dir(p)` | `stderr_dir` | path |
| `no_stderr` | `no_stderr` | none |
| `progress(…)` | `sink(Progress)` | `marks = unicode|ascii|none`, `color = auto|always|never`, `rewrite = auto|always|never`, `stream = stdout|stderr` |
| `table(p, …)` | `sink(Table)` | path, `mode = whole|ragged|blocks(headers = once|each|whole)` |

### Step

| attribute | builder | arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `jobs(n)` | `batched` | integer. Absent means serial |
| `on_error(v)` | `on_error` | `continue`, `skip`, `abort` |
| `cores(n)` | `cores` | integer |
| `memory(v)` | `memory` | `preferred`, `bound`, `first_touch` |
| `pool(n)` | `pool` | integer |

The step's name is on its header, `step burn`, and may be omitted:
`step { … }`.

### Command

| attribute | builder | arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name(s)` | `name` | string |
| `cores(n)` | `cores` | integer |
| `sub(s)` | `sub` | string |
| `memory(v)` | `memory` | as on a step |
| `env(K = v, …)` | `env` | keys and values |
| `dir(p)` | `dir` | path |
| `timeout(d)` | `timeout` | duration |
| `stdout(v)`, `stderr(v)` | `stdout`, `stderr` | `null`, `inherit`, `file(p)`, `append(p)`, `on_failure(p)` |
| `stdout_to(p)`, `stderr_to(p)` | `stdout_to`, `stderr_to` | path |
| `field(k = v, …)` | `field` | keys and values. A positional `$N` records N under its own name |
| `tag(s)` | `tag` | string |

notes.author: Jack Roddy/a556920e
notes.text:
Design: commands. Agreed 2026-10-08.

Inside a step, a command is shell text from its first token to the next
unquoted `;`. It may span lines. `cmd1; cmd2` is two commands, each its
own process and its own table row. michi hands the text to `/bin/sh -c`
after the steps below, and the table's argv column shows the text as
written.

To find the `;`, michi scans with the shell's quoting in mind. A `;` is
the shell's, not a terminator, inside single or double quotes, after a
backslash, inside `$(…)`, `${…}`, `(…)` or `{…}`, and inside backticks. A
`}` with no `{` open, or a `#[` at the start of a line, means the `;` was
left out, and michi says so at load rather than reading the next step's
header as part of the command.

A command cannot begin with `<`, since that opens a parameter list. Write
`sort < in.txt` rather than `< in.txt sort`.

Before the text reaches the shell:

1. michi removes a `#` comment: a `#` at the start of a word, outside
   quotes, to the end of its physical line. `//` is not a comment
   inside a command, since `http://` and `a//b` are shell.
2. michi replaces newlines outside quotes with spaces, so a wrapped
   command is one shell command. A newline inside quotes stays.
3. michi substitutes sweep variables, as below.

A raw string is a command too: `r#"for f in *.txt; do wc -l $f; done"#;`.
michi hands it over without the scanning or the joining, so it may hold
its own `;`, a heredoc, or a `case`. Substitution still applies to it.

A command's first word, after substitution, is its default label.

### Substitution

michi replaces `$N` and `${N}` in command text, in a string, or as a bare
attribute argument with the current value of N when N is a sweep
variable. Any other `$x` reaches the shell untouched, so `$HOME`,
`$(…)` and `$f` inside a raw-string loop keep working.

The splice is textual. A value with a space in it splits as it would in
shell, and the author quotes it as in shell: `"$Q"`.

michi never substitutes `\$N`, and the backslash reaches the shell, whose
own rules for `\$` then apply: a literal `$N` outside single quotes.

### Paths

A relative path in an attribute or a command is relative to the working
directory of the `michi` process, as it is for `sbatch` and `make`. The
`dir` attribute sets a command's own working directory.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/a556920e
notes.text:
Design: sweeps. Agreed 2026-10-08.

A parameter list, `<…>`, sits on a step header or on a bare block, and
repeats the contents of that block once per point.

| form | means |
| --- | --- |
| `<N = [5, 10, 15]>` | declare N with its list inline |
| `<quick.N>` | declare N from the data block, named by the last segment |
| `<M = quick.N>` | the same list under another name |
| `<N, K>` | a product, N outer, K inner |
| `<(N, LABEL) = sizes.POINTS>` | a tuple list, the variables advance together |

Inside the block, `$N` is the current value. One name inside and out.

The shorthand on a tuple list, `<sizes.POINTS>`, is an error: a tuple
list needs the pattern form. Declaring a name already bound by an
enclosing block is an error. A `$N` inside a list literal in a parameter
list is not allowed.

What is repeated depends on where the list sits:

| where the list sits | effect |
| --- | --- |
| `step burn<N> { … }` | one step, its body repeated per point |
| `<N> { step burn { … } }` | one step per point |
| `<N> { … }` inside a step | that command or group repeated per point |
| `<N> { pipeline … }` | forbidden |

michi labels the items directly inside the repeated block by their
instantiation, with no spaces: `burn<5,a>`, `seq<5,a>`. The table pads
columns with whitespace, so a label never holds a space. A `name`
attribute overrides the label.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/a556920e
notes.text:
Design: how the parser works. Agreed 2026-10-08.

A hand-written lexer and recursive descent parser, with no dependencies.
The lexer has two entry points: the next michi token, or a scan of command
text to its `;` under the shell quoting rules above, which the parser asks
for once it knows it is looking at a command. Four passes, in this order,
because an attribute argument cannot be typed until its sweep variable is
bound.

1. Parse: tokens to an untyped tree. An attribute is a name and a list of
   argument values.
2. Resolve: look up data references and evaluate ranges. Sweeps stay as
   written. The `.sh` script comes from this tree.
3. Expand: bind each parameter list to each of its points, copy the block
   per point, replace every `$N` token, splice `$N` into strings and
   command text, assign labels.
4. Lower: map each attribute to its builder method and type its arguments.

The parser stops at the first error.

michi reports every error at load, before anything runs, with the file
and line, and with the binding when a sweep is involved: `line 68, for
T = a: cores takes an integer`.
